title: "08 · Model building"

::: {.guiding-q}
How do I build a good model?
:::

## In this session

- Models follow from the research question, not from the data
- Choosing predictors and control variables: causal reasoning and DAGs
- Non-linear effects with polynomials and transformations
- Simulating data from your planned model to check design and power
- Writing down the model *before* data collection (link to the course [Open, Replicable, and Ethical Science](../../ores/index.qmd))

::: {.key-terms}
**Key terms:** [Polynomial term](../../glossary.qmd#polynomial), [Power](../../glossary.qmd#power), [Preregistration](../../glossary.qmd#preregistration)
:::

## Learning goals

After this session you can

- derive a model from a research question and justify each term,
- recognise when to include a quadratic term or transform a variable,
- run a simple power analysis by simulation.

## Simulate first

Power analysis by simulation: how often do we detect a slope of 0.3 with *n* animals?

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.2
set.seed(8)
power_for_n <- function(n, b1 = 0.3, nsim = 500) {
  mean(replicate(nsim, {
    x <- rnorm(n); y <- b1 * x + rnorm(n)
    summary(lm(y ~ x))$coefficients[2, 4] < .05
  }))
}
ns  <- seq(10, 120, by = 10)
pow <- sapply(ns, power_for_n)

plot(ns, pow, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "#1b6f8a", ylim = c(0, 1),
     xlab = "Sample size", ylab = "Power")
abline(h = .8, lty = 2, col = "#c0392b")
```
